what_its_for: Upadacitinib is used to treat several conditions where your immune system is overactive and causing inflammation. These include rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis (a type of spine arthritis), atopic dermatitis (eczema), ulcerative colitis, and Crohn's disease. It works by blocking certain proteins (called JAK enzymes) that trigger inflammation in your body.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablet whole with or without food. Do NOT crush, split, or chew the tablet — it must be swallowed whole to work correctly. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. You can take it in the morning or evening, whichever works best for your routine.
dosing: The dose depends on the condition being treated. Common doses are 15 mg once daily for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and ankylosing spondylitis. For atopic dermatitis (eczema), doses can range from 15 mg to 30 mg once daily. For ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, your doctor may start you on a higher induction dose (45 mg once daily for up to 12 weeks) and then reduce it to a maintenance dose of 15 mg or 30 mg once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at your regular scheduled time. Never take two doses in one day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store upadacitinib at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in its original container and out of direct sunlight and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications safely out of reach of children and pets. Do not use tablets past their expiration date printed on the bottle.
what_to_avoid: Avoid contact with people who have active infections, including colds, flu, or chickenpox, as this medication lowers your immune system's ability to fight infections. Do not receive live vaccines (such as live shingles vaccine, MMV, or live flu nasal spray) while taking this medication — talk to your doctor about which vaccines are safe. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen, as this medicine may slightly increase your risk of skin cancer. Limit or avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice as it may affect how the drug works in your body. Avoid smoking, which can increase your risk of serious side effects including heart problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of infection such as fever, chills, sweating, cough, shortness of breath, or painful urination; chest pain or pressure, sudden numbness or weakness, or difficulty speaking (signs of heart attack or stroke); unusual lumps or skin changes that could suggest new cancers; severe stomach pain, bloody stools, or changes in bowel habits; signs of a blood clot such as swelling, warmth, or redness in your leg, or sudden shortness of breath; liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe tiredness; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Many patients start to notice some improvement in symptoms within 2 to 4 weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take 3 to 6 months of regular use to feel the full benefit of this medication. Be patient and continue taking it as directed even if you do not notice immediate changes. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medication is NOT recommended during pregnancy as it may harm the unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 4 weeks after your last dose. Tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Do not breastfeed while taking this medication. Older Adults (65+): You may have a higher risk of serious infections, heart problems, and certain cancers. Your doctor will monitor you more closely. Kidney or Liver Problems: Dose adjustments may be needed if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver problems. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Children: Upadacitinib is approved for adolescents 12 years and older for atopic dermatitis. Safety and dosing in younger children has not been fully established for all conditions.
